chapter: New Orleans clubs and Sharky's band
title: How he and Allen first met; Sharky's band at 910 Bourbon
summary: Recalls meeting Allen at a Royal Street shoeshine in 1965 and Allen hearing Sharky's band in 1949.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I've heard you with so many different bands, it's hard for me to keep it straight, you know, who all of them were. Because you've been coming here for so many years. I guess I first heard you in 1949. I may have heard you in 45. I was down here in the Navy.

I just don't quite remember. Well, I can tell you one thing, that when I first really got to know you, and you will never remember this, but I will, because I've got a complete tattoo mind. Once it's there, it's there, and it never leaves, hardly. We were both getting a shoeshine on Royal Street. Oh, I remember that. You remember that conversation we had, and you told me that you knew my brother Johnny and all, and you talked to him.
Yeah, I think that was in 65. See there?
I had known you a long time before.
But we never did actually get to talk very much together.
I think I was probably busy talking to Santa about trombone or something. When I'd come to the famous door.

That's right. I remember seeing you, but we never did really get to know each other until that conversation that we had. And when you mentioned the fact that you had talked to my brother Johnny, it made an impression on me, and it never did leave me. You know it didn't leave me because I just brought it back up.

Yeah. Of course, and I'd been collecting the records with the Razor Crested City Jazz. I knew that that you were good. I knew that you were good. Because Raymond sold me so many wonderful records. And I guess I knew Raymond better than anybody else in Shockey's band when I came in because I was trying to buy all these records and things, and he would come on.
It was a little place on Bourbon Street in the 900 block, wasn't it?
Yeah, 910 Bourbon Street. He's a character. Oh, yeah.

But when I first came to town, Pam, in September of 1949, I would go every night to hear Jeff, even if I couldn't afford to buy a drink in the place, with Shockey's band. And that's when Lester Bouchon had an operation then. You remember that? And Raymond took his place. And Raymond took his place. And, of course, I was... I guess I had gotten to know Raymond.
